setup: Bar end in a landmine or a padded corner
Stand side-on, front foot nearest the bar
Hinge until your torso is near flat
Free forearm on your front thigh
execution: Grip the bar just behind the plates
Pull your elbow back toward your hip
Keep your chest square to the floor
Lower slowly to a full stretch
faults: Don't stand up tall to pull
Don't twist your torso to lift

notes: Hold a flat back through the hinge; your free arm on your thigh is the only support for your upper body.
Use small plates (or straps) if grip on the thick bar end fails before your back does.
Make sure the landmine or corner is secure so the bar can't slide.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

keyPositions.label: Stretch
keyPositions.describe: Staggered stance side-on to the bar, front foot nearest it. Hips hinged so the torso is close to parallel with the floor, back flat. Free forearm on the front thigh. Working arm hanging long, gripping the bar just behind the plates, shoulder blade reaching down.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Elbow pulled up and back toward the hip, bar end beside the lower ribs. Torso still hinged and square to the floor; no twist.
